app.title: Interview transcript coder
app.summary: A person reads one interview transcript at a time as numbered speaker turns, selects a passage inside a turn and clicks a code in the codebook beside it, and the passage stays tinted in that code's colour; a passage can carry more than one code, and any code can be taken off again. The codebook shows each code's definition with how many segments it covers and in how many participants, and new codes can be added with a name and definition as coding goes on. A code's filter gathers every turn with that code across all transcripts, each labelled with its source and linked back to its place in the full transcript. Coding is kept in the browser, and the coded segments export as a spreadsheet of source, turn, speaker, code and quoted text.

task.text: Apply codes from a growing codebook to passages of interview transcripts and see how widely each code is spread across participants.

data.text: Interview transcripts split into speaker turns, a codebook of named codes with definitions, and coded segments that tie a stretch of one turn to a code.
data.item: a passage within one speaker turn of an interview transcript

stage.text: first-pass and inductive coding in a thematic analysis

mechanism.text: A transcript reader fills the main area and a codebook sidebar sits beside it: text selected within a turn waits in the sidebar until a code name is clicked, then the coded stretch is tinted in the reader with a removable chip beside the turn. A code's filter button swaps the reader for every turn carrying that code across all transcripts, each with a button back to its place in the full transcript.

field.text: thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews in HCI

workflow.name: apply codes from a codebook to passages of text

steps.here: A tab per participant opens that interview as numbered speaker turns, with interviewer turns muted and the participant's coded-segment count at the top.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Text selected inside one turn waits in the Selected passage box; clicking a code's name in the codebook applies it, the stretch stays tinted in that code's colour, and a chip beside the turn lists the code with an x to take it off again.

steps.step: add a new category as the work goes
steps.here: A form under the codebook adds a code with a name and a definition, gives it the next unused colour, and refuses a name already in the codebook.

steps.step: count each category's items and how many sources they come from
steps.here: Each code in the sidebar shows its number of coded segments, how many participants it appears in, and a count per participant, next to its definition.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A code's Show turns button replaces the transcript with every turn carrying that code across all participants, each labelled with participant and turn number and a button that opens it in place in the full transcript.
Every coded segment downloads as a CSV row of participant, turn, speaker, code and quoted text, in transcript order.

distinctive: A passage can carry two codes at once; the overlap shows as the first code's tint with an underline in the second code's colour.
A coded passage must sit inside one speaker turn; a selection that crosses speakers is refused.
The codebook grows during coding: new codes with a name and definition are added from the sidebar, and every definition stays in view beside its code.
Each code's spread is counted per participant, so a code that comes from one talkative participant stands apart from one that everyone mentions.
Coding and added codes are saved in the browser, so work survives a restart.
